Price Display: Sliding scale by family income: free for family AGI ≤$120,000; $2,000 ($120-150K); $4,000 ($150-200K); $8,000 ($200-400K); $20,000 (≥$400K); further aid available if these amounts are a hardship
Description: Highly selective four-week residential engineering program at MIT for young women and other underrepresented/underserved students in engineering; hands-on classes, labs, and team projects in mechanical engineering, taught by MIT graduate students with undergraduate assistants living in the dorm. No prior engineering background expected or desired.
Review Notes: 2027 session dates (Jun 26-Jul 24) and Oct 16 application open date confirmed on wtp.mit.edu homepage; intake draft had predated that publication. EECS track has been on hiatus since 2022 (following the retirement of longtime director Cynthia Skier) - only the ME track currently runs. Eligibility is unusually strict: must be a CURRENT 11th grader at time of application (not rising senior framing used elsewhere), and family's permanent home address must be in the US year-round even if the student attends school abroad; conversely a student attending a US school is ineligible if the family home is outside the US. ~20 spots selected from an applicant pool that has ranged from ~190 to 650+ in recent years.
